title: Interpreter

act2.summary: a new operator and a new term

solutions.title: Terminal and nonterminal expression objects, parsed once into a tree
solutions.tradeoff: Every clause becomes an object with an evaluate method instead of a branch in one function - a new operator or term is one new lookup-table entry, not a new if-chain to get the substring matching right, but a one-clause constraint now allocates three objects (a comparison or flag, wrapped in an AndExpression) to do what a single string comparison did.

reviewFocus: Does anything outside parse.ts know that a clause is a string before it becomes an expression object?
Is ComparisonExpression parameterized by operator and field, or does adding >= to OPERATORS require touching that class at all?
Does the operator lookup in parse.ts sort by length before matching - and what breaks if it doesn't, the moment <= exists alongside <?
Is AndExpression's evaluate() method the only place && is meaningful, or does anything else assume clauses are joined that way?
Given how rarely a real interpreter needs a full grammar like this, what would have to be true about the constraint language for this route to earn its keep over the string-matching baseline?
